Trigger an on-demand check for a standing agent — the design's "Run a
check". Queues a run that the EXISTING scheduler/worker claims and executes
through the SAME bounded, zero-tools, read-only loop the scheduled cadence
uses (this endpoint never runs the loop inline, never grants tools, and never
relaxes the max-steps / token / wall-clock bounds — those are re-pinned from

is retired, or belongs to another tenant returns 404 (no existence leak — we
never reveal whether the id is real for a different tenant).

pending/leased/running (scheduled OR manual), this returns 409
``run_already_in_flight`` rather than queuing a second — the shared agent
inference lane must not be floodable.

Works for any cadence: a 'manual' agent (next_run_at = NULL, never
auto-runs) is the primary case, but "run a check now" on a scheduled agent is
equally valid and does NOT perturb its next_run_at.

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible audio transcription.

Drop-in replacement for `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions`.

**Models live:**
- `whisper-large-v3-turbo` — OpenAI Whisper large-v3-turbo, 100+ languages,
  automatic language detection.

**Request:** `multipart/form-data` with required `file` field. Optional
`language` (ISO-639-1 hint), `prompt` (text bias), `temperature`,
`response_format`.

**Response formats:**
- `json` (default) — `{"text": "..."}`.
- `verbose_json` — adds `language`, `duration`, and per-segment timestamps.
- `text` — plain transcribed text only.

**Billing:** £0.005 per audio minute, billed on the actual audio duration
(not file size). A 6-second clip is 0.1 minutes = £0.0005.

**Limits:**
- File size: 200 MB max.
- Duration: 30 minutes max per request.
- Supported formats: any audio/video the upstream Whisper can decode
  (mp3, mp4, m4a, wav, webm, flac, ogg, etc.).

get.description:
SSE endpoint that streams transcripts from the Redis tailpipe.

Replaces the previous pattern of "client keeps the audio WS open
until WhisperLive finishes." After PR #48 shipped the band-aid
30 s drain, this is the proper architecture: the audio WS closes
immediately after the client receives the eos_ack, and the
transcripts arrive over a fresh HTTP/SSE stream keyed by job_id.

The Redis tailpipe (`voice:job:{job_id}:msgs` + `:meta`) survives
the audio WS closing AND the gateway restarting (within TTL). A
user who navigates away during processing and comes back can
re-open the SSE stream and get their transcript — the message
list and meta are both content-addressable by job_id.

Auth: same `require_billable_auth` as the audio WS. Codex R1
HIGH #3: ALSO tenant-binds the job — the bridge writes the
owning tenant_id at init_job time, and this handler verifies
the requesting tenant matches before opening the stream. A
leaked job_id URL (browser history, support dumps, referrers,
logs) is no longer enough to read someone else's transcript.

Lifecycle:
  * If the job_id is unknown / expired, return 404 immediately
    rather than open an infinite empty stream (better DX, better
    for monitoring).
  * Otherwise, open the SSE stream and poll Redis every 200 ms.
    Emit each new message as `event: transcript\ndata: <json>`.
    When meta marks complete, emit `event: done\ndata: {...}`
    and close.
  * Hard ceiling of 180 s (`_VOICE_RESULT_MAX_STREAM_S`) — past
    that, emit `event: done\ndata: {"status":"timeout"}` so the
    client can decide to reopen.

Disconnects (client closes the SSE early) raise on the next send
inside `_stream()` and we exit cleanly — the Redis state remains
available for a later reconnect.

post.description:
Create a Stripe Checkout session for a credit top-up.

Returns a Stripe Checkout `url` for the client to redirect to. The
top-up is credited to the tenant's balance asynchronously after Stripe
confirms payment (typically within seconds of card authorisation).

**Required body fields:**
- `amount_pence` (int) — top-up amount in pence. Range: 500 (£5.00) to
  1,000,000 (£10,000.00).
- `client_idempotency_key` (str, 8–128 chars) — caller-supplied
  idempotency key. Reusing the same key returns the SAME Checkout
  Session URL — prevents double-charges from double-clicked Pay buttons.

**Optional body fields:**
- `currency` — defaults to `"gbp"` (only currency supported in v1).
- `success_url` / `cancel_url` — Stripe redirect URLs. Default to the
  GPUBox dashboard.

**Response:**
- `id` — Stripe Checkout Session ID.
- `url` — Stripe Checkout URL to redirect the user to.
- `amount_pence`, `currency`, `expires_at` — session metadata.
- `idempotent_replay` (bool, optional) — `true` if this call returned an
  existing pending session for the same idempotency key.

Receipt emails are sent to the tenant's billing email after payment clears.

Start an NGN credit top-up via Paystack.

Returns a Paystack `authorization_url` for the client to redirect to.
Credit is added to the tenant's balance asynchronously after Paystack
confirms payment via webhook (typically seconds after card auth).

**Required body fields:**
- `amount_kobo` (int) — top-up amount in NGN kobo. Range: 100,000 (₦1,000)
  to 500,000,000 (₦5,000,000). Higher caps require BVN/KYC capture
  (deferred).
- `client_idempotency_key` (str, 8–128 chars) — caller-supplied
  idempotency key. Reusing the same key returns the SAME
  authorization_url — prevents double-charges from double-clicked Pay
  buttons.

**Optional body fields:**
- `currency` — defaults to `"ngn"` (only currency Paystack accepts).
- `callback_url` — override the default redirect-after-payment URL.

**Response:**
- `authorization_url` — Paystack hosted-checkout URL to redirect to.
- `reference` — Paystack transaction reference (also our provider_reference).
- `amount_kobo` — what you'll be charged in NGN minor units.
- `credited_amount_pence` — GBP credit you'll receive (computed at the
   FX rate published right now; locked in once you submit).
- `currency` — `"ngn"`.
- `idempotent_replay` (bool, optional) — `true` if this returned an
  existing pending session for the same idempotency key.

Kick off a subscription via the country-appropriate payment rail.

- `country` (str, 2 chars) — market code, "UK" or "NG". The chat
  frontend derives this from the URL host. The gateway treats it
  as a routing key only; **no IP geo lookup is performed**.
- `plan` (str) — currently "unlimited" only.

**Response (provider-specific shape, normalized to a common envelope):**
```json
{
  "checkout_url": "<provider-hosted-checkout URL>",
  "currency": "gbp" | "ngn",
  "amount": 2000,
  "provider": "stripe" | "paystack",
  "plan_id": "unlimited",
  "country": "UK" | "NG"
}
```

- 400 `invalid_country` — country not in the supported set.
- 400 `invalid_plan` — plan not in the supported set.
- 401 — no session cookie and no valid bearer.
- 503 `billing_unavailable` — provider not configured on this server.

schema — your existing OpenAI SDK code works against `https://api.gpubox.ai/v1`
with one base-URL change.

**Models live:**
- `qwen2.5-32b-instruct` — Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (AWQ-int4), 8k context.
- `llama-3.3-70b-instruct` — Llama 3.3 70B Instruct, 128k context.

  multimodal, 8k context. Send images as `image_url` content parts

- Streaming via Server-Sent Events (`stream: true`). The final chunk
  includes a `usage` object with token counts.
- Tool / function calling (`tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`).
- JSON mode (`response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`).

chattable RAG corpus.

One call: file bytes -> sovereign text extraction (markitdown: PDF, DOCX,
PPTX, XLSX, text, CSV, JSON; scanned-PDF/image OCR when the operator has
configured the sovereign VLM) -> sentence-aware chunks -> embedded into a
corpus. The corpus is then chattable via the `X-GPUBox-RAG` header on
/v1/chat/completions or retrievable via POST /v1/rag/retrieve.

  * CREATE (default): omit `corpus_id`, pass `corpus_name` — a new corpus is
    created from this document.
  * APPEND: pass an existing `corpus_id` — the document's chunks are appended
    (e.g. add several CVs to one job corpus).

corpus is the per-customer / per-job / per-candidate container. Create one
corpus per unit of isolation and tag it via `metadata` (e.g.
{"customer_id": "...", "job_id": "..."}). All corpora are tenant-scoped by
RLS; the integrator maps its customer -> corpus_id and enforces that mapping
in its own app layer.

Extraction failures surface as HTTP errors, never a 201 with empty content:
  * 415 — file type/size the extractor cannot handle ('unsupported').
  * 422 — extraction attempted but failed: corrupt/mismatched container,
    too many chunks, or OCR error ('errored').

post.description:
Promote a 'succeeded' + 'replicated' training run to a hosted model.

Steps:
  1. Validate the training run exists, is owned by this tenant, has
     status='succeeded' AND durability='replicated' (Kimi rule —
     not-yet-replicated artifacts cannot be promoted).
  2. Enforce the per-tenant tier cap (max_*_models columns).
  3. INSERT the row at status='provisioning'.
  4. If always_hot or warm: ask vLLM to load the adapter now. On 200,
     flip status='ready'. On failure, flip 'error' and surface a 503.
  5. If cold: skip the vLLM call, flip 'ready' immediately (loaded
     on demand from /v1/chat/completions).

List available models. OpenAI-compatible response shape.

Only models currently serving requests are returned. Models marked
"coming soon" on https://gpubox.ai/models/ are NOT in this list yet
(they'd 503) — they appear here when their endpoint is live.

upstream is configured (either explicit in GPUBOX_VLLM_UPSTREAMS or
synthesised via GPUBOX_VLLM_LLAMA_URL). V1.1 — QwQ-32B follows the
same rule via the `qwq`-role pool. W3 — Qwen2.5-VL-7B (vision /
image-understanding) follows it too via the `vision`-role pool
(GPUBOX_VLLM_VISION_URL); send images as `image_url` content parts.

the docstring promise above ("only models currently serving") is
load-bearing for SDK introspection; advertising a model whose
upstream is unwired would break that contract and confuse callers
that filter the `/v1/models` list to pick a model. The chat handler
still surfaces 503 + X-GPUBox-Breaker-Role-Unavailable for any
`model: "llama-..."` / `model: "qwq-..."` request when the upstream
isn't there.

get.description:
Poll the status of a delete (purge or crypto-shred) job.

AUTH (Codex slice-5 R4 BLOCKER):
  * EITHER all four signed-URL query params (tenant_id, exp, kid,
    sig) — HMAC-verified against the PR-0C tenant-export keyring
    scope. Used post-quiesce when the bearer would be rejected by
    the auth resolver (the purge handler flips is_active=false at
    the top, and every auth path then 403s the tenant). The
    signed URL is minted at enqueue time + returned in the 202
    response.
  * OR a human-admin bearer. Useful before the purge handler has
    started OR for crypto-shred (the cryptoshred handler does NOT
    flip is_active=false).

Response shape matches the export poll, minus
signed_download_url (delete jobs have no artifact).

post.description:
Enqueue a tenant data-export job.

Returns 202 with the job id + a polling URL. The PR-0B
idempotency middleware caches the 202 response so a retry with
the same Idempotency-Key returns the same job_id.

Defence-in-depth: even if the middleware was somehow bypassed,
the schema's partial UNIQUE on (tenant_id, idempotency_key)
catches the duplicate enqueue at INSERT time; the endpoint
catches the UniqueViolationError and returns the existing
job_id.

get.description:
Poll the status of an export job.

Returns the job's current state + a signed download URL when
status='complete'. The signed URL is valid for ~1h (see
DEFAULT_URL_TTL_SECONDS in app/tenant_export.py).

Cross-tenant defence: the WHERE clause requires the job's
tenant_id == auth.tenant_id, so a path-param job_id from
another tenant returns 404 rather than leaking shape.

Stream the export bundle bytes for a completed job.

AUTH: signed-URL ONLY — NO bearer required. The query-string
components (tenant_id, exp, kid, sig) are HMAC-verified against
the PR-0C keyring scope 'tenant-export'. Tampered / expired /
wrong-kid URLs return 403.

Cross-tenant defence in depth: AFTER the HMAC check passes, the
endpoint reads the job row and asserts row.tenant_id == query
tenant_id. A signed URL minted for tenant A cannot stream
tenant B's bundle even if the signature is somehow valid.

Streams the bytes from the job row's payload._bundle_b64 field.
V2 will redirect to an Object Storage signed URL instead.

Per-modality usage counters for the current billing period.

Window: **calendar month, UTC**. Aligns with monthly Stripe/Paystack
subscription cycles so the meter matches the invoice the customer
will receive — not a rolling 30d smoothing window.

READ-ONLY. Does NOT decrement balance, does NOT show caps (caps
land W5a), does NOT bill. Single GBP-pence balance on
`/v1/billing/balance` remains authoritative for enforcement.

Returns:
- `period_start` / `period_end` — ISO-8601 UTC bounds of the calendar
  month, half-open `[start, end)`.
- `modalities` — dict keyed by `chat` / `audio` / `embed` / `image` /
  `video`. Each value has:
    - `units` — sum of `gpubox_usage_events.units` for this modality,
      FLOORED to int for display (tokens are always integer in v1;
      audio is sub-second — see `units_precise`).
    - `units_precise` — exact Decimal sum serialized as a string
      (`"12.9"`), mirroring `balance.py`'s `balance_pence_precise`
      shape. Use this for accounting / charts that aggregate.
      Without it `int(SUM(0.4))` over hundreds of sub-second audio
      requests would drop the entire month's audio total to zero.
    - `request_count` — number of finalized requests.
    - `unit_type` — e.g. `"tokens"` for chat/embed,
      `"audio_seconds"` for audio. UI uses this to render the right
      label next to the number; without it "3600" for audio would
      be ambiguous. The default value (used when no events exist
      this period) MATCHES the writer's value, so zero-month and
      non-zero-month responses use the same label.
  `image` / `video` are always zero in v1 — their writers ship in
  W3+ — but the keys are present so the UsageMeter component
  renders the full strip without conditional keys.
- `excluded_request_count` — count of finalized requests NOT
  bucketed into a modality (`/v1/training/runs` is the only excluded
  endpoint today; training has GPU-hour semantics + its own
  dashboard). Operator-facing sanity check.

delete.description:
Tombstone a document the tenant owns + stamp a 30-day hard-purge
deadline. GDPR Art.17 right-to-erasure.

Read/erase path — gated on the hardened flag but NOT on the Vault
entitlement: a lapsed tenant must always be able to delete their own
data (you can't paywall erasure). Tenant-scoped at the repo (RLS GUC +
explicit tenant_id predicate), so a document owned by another tenant
is invisible and resolves to 404.

Returns:
  * 204 — the document was live and is now tombstoned.
  * 404 — no live document with that id is owned by the tenant
          (never existed, already deleted, or owned by someone else).
          Idempotent-safe: a second DELETE of an already-deleted row
          returns 404 without re-stamping the purge deadline.

get.description:
Resolve ONE document's indexing lifecycle, by id.

WHY THIS EXISTS
---------------
The chat composer chip needs a cheap, targeted poll keyed by the doc id it
already holds, so it can watch ONE upload walk scanning -> ... -> ready
without re-paging the whole workspace list every few seconds. This route is
that path: it resolves a single doc via repo.get_document and returns the
rolled-up `indexing_state` the chip polls until 'ready' / 'failed'.
(Historically the list endpoint also EXCLUDED kind='chat' docs, so the list
couldn't observe a chat doc at all; that carve-out was relaxed in option A,
2026-06-26, but the by-id poll remains the right read path for a live chip.)

POSTURE
-------
* Read path — gated on the hardened flag like its siblings, but NOT on the
  per-tenant Vault entitlement: a FREE chat-attachment doc MUST be
  status-pollable (same posture as list_documents + the download route).
* Tenant + workspace scoped at the repo (RLS GUC + explicit tenant_id AND
  workspace_id predicates in get_document). A doc owned by another tenant
  OR living in another workspace is invisible and resolves to 404 — never
  403 — so the route leaks nothing about a foreign id's existence (keeps
  the workspace-isolation boundary, #373, and the SKU boundary clean).
* A malformed (non-UUID) id resolves to 404 BEFORE the repo runs, matching
  delete_document — a bad id can never name an owned row.

Returns:
  * 200 — the document is owned + visible; body carries its status.
  * 404 — no live document with that id is owned by the tenant in the
          active workspace (never existed, deleted, foreign, or malformed).

post.description:
Fetch 1..5 public web pages and extract structured data described by `capture` (or shaped by an optional `schema`). This is the PREVIEW path: it returns the extracted records but writes NOTHING to the vault. To persist accepted records, call POST /v1/vault/enrich/save.

The call is partial-success tolerant: each URL yields its own record with a per-record `status`; a blocked or failed URL does not fail the whole request.

**Gating flags.** The route is enabled only when `GPUBOX_VAULT_ENRICH_ENABLED` is on AND the extractor URL + JWT secret are configured (otherwise 404 `not_enabled`). Setting `save: true` returns 400 `save_gated` (use the save route); setting `webhook` returns 400 `webhook_not_supported` (async delivery lands in VE-W2).

post.description:
Persist 1..5 web-enrichment records the user accepted from a /v1/vault/enrich preview as RAG-indexed vault documents.

**Gating flags.** Requires BOTH `GPUBOX_VAULT_HARDENED_ENABLED` and `GPUBOX_VAULT_ENRICH_SAVE_ENABLED` (otherwise 404 `save_not_enabled`). The tenant must also hold the Vault entitlement + PII consent (else 403 `vault_not_enabled` / `vault_pii_consent_missing`).

Partial-success tolerant: a per-record render error / oversized blob / already-saved duplicate lands that record under `skipped` with a reason while the rest of the batch saves. The whole request fails only on auth, collection-ownership (400 `invalid_collection`), or flag errors.
